transcript.text: “Not working” can mean a few different faults: a power/door or programme-start issue, a drum-drive fault, or it may run but not heat or dry. The quickest way to separate those is: when you select a normal drying programme and press Start, does anything happen at all—display/lights on, a click or hum, drum turning, or does it stay completely dead? Before checking anything physical, switch it off and unplug it.
Lights come on, programme lights too, but nothing happens when I press start. No sound at all, drum doesn't turn. No error showing.

As the controls light up but there is no click, hum or drum movement when Start is pressed, the first suspects are that the dryer is not recognising the door as shut, or a child-lock/delay setting is preventing a start. Less commonly, it is the Start control or main control board. With the dryer switched off and unplugged, check that no fluff or fabric is caught in the door catch and that the door closes firmly with a click. Then reconnect it: is a padlock/key symbol or a delay countdown showing, and does it start after shutting the door firmly?

No padlock or countdown showing. The door doesn't click when I shut it, it swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

The snapped plastic tongue is the cause: it cannot hold the door closed, so the door safety switch opens as soon as you let go and stops the dryer. The likely repair is the door catch/handle part that includes that tongue; the exact arrangement varies by model. Do not run it while holding the door shut or try to wedge/bypass the switch. Send the brand and full model number and I can help identify whether it is normally a handle/catch repair or one needing an engineer.
It's a Hotpoint. I don't know the model number offhand, I can read it from inside the door recess if you need it. Want me to?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Yes, please—read the full model number from the sticker inside the door opening/recess. The broken door tongue is the clear cause here, and the model number will let us narrow down whether the replacement is the complete door handle/catch assembly or a separate catch part. If you cannot get to the label right now, it can wait; don’t use the dryer by holding or wedging the door shut.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I'll go and look now. I don't have the number yet, will tell you when I've read it.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The broken door tongue/handle catch is the clear fault: the dryer starts only while the door is physically held shut, then stops as the door opens back out. Please send the full Hotpoint model number once you have read the label in the door recess; it will help identify whether the repair is a complete handle/catch assembly or a separate catch piece. Keep the dryer out of use rather than holding or wedging the door shut.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Ok, I've got it, but I'm not sure what you want me to do with it. What should I do next?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The next step is simply to send me the full model number from that label—type it exactly as printed, including any letters, numbers and hyphens. The broken door tongue/handle catch is the clear cause: the dryer will run only while the door is held shut because the safety switch is no longer kept engaged. With the model number, I can narrow down whether the correct repair is a complete door-handle/catch assembly or a separate latch piece. Keep it out of use for now; do not hold or wedge the door shut to run it.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
